newsitem.title: USA: Honda to build S. Carolina plant -- local officials.
newsitem.headline: Honda to build S. Carolina plant -- local officials.

text.p: Honda Motor Co. Ltd. plans to build a $40 million plant here that will produce all-terrain vehicles and personal watercraft, local officials said Thursday.

Timmonsville Mayor Henry Peoples said Honda plans to announce plans for the facility near Florence, S.C., on Monday. It is expected to be built in five phases, with the first phase employing about 600 workers, he said.
The first-phase products will include the watercraft and motorcycle-like ATVs, but Peoples said Honda has not disclosed products for later phases of the facility.

Honda spokesman Roger Lambert said only that the company planned to make an announcement soon regarding its U.S. manufacturing operations, and added that Honda was not announcing plans for a new car assembly plant.
"There will be more information in the very near future," he said.
In addition to its car plants in Marysville and East Liberty, Ohio, and Alliston, Ontario, Honda also produces motorcycles and ATVs in Marysville and lawn mowers in Swepsonville, N.C.
Honda currently does not build personal watercraft anywhere in the world. The U.S. market for such watercraft has grown rapidly in recent years, but recently has shown some signs of leveling off.
Earlier, South Carolina Sen. Ernest Hollings, a Democrat, discused the plant during a meeting of the Senate Commerce Committee. His office said the facility would employ about 700 people.

Peoples said the state, county and town governments have assembled an incentive package for Honda, but he declined to disclose its value. The plant will be located near the intersection of Interstate highways 95 and 20.
"We are just as excited as we can be," Peoples said of the project.
